scores.rationale: All requested features present: 30x30 grid (GRID_SIZE=30, 20px cells on a 600px canvas), continuous movement, growth on eating, wall/self collision ending the game, WASD + arrow-key controls, a BFS-pathfinding CPU snake, all three modes (human-human, cpu-human, cpu-cpu), live score board, start menu, game-over screen and R-to-restart.

No console errors and controls/animation clearly work (interact-3 shows snakes advanced, interact-2 shows the game-over screen), but gameplay is broken in practice: both snakes spawn on row 15 facing each other 19 cells apart, so with no or normal input the game ends in about one second — interact-2 shows 'GAME OVER / Player 1 hit Player 2!' with 0-0 scores after only ~4.5s of play including two keypresses. There is also no way to restart with R during play (restartGame() is gated on isGameOver), so interact-3's R press does nothing.

Coherent dark theme, readable green/blue player colours, subtle grid, tidy centred menu and overlay panels; plain and unremarkable rather than polished, and the game-over panel covers most of the board, but no visual defects.

Reasonable sectioning and naming, but a lot of copy-paste: snake1/snake2 are two parallel globals rather than an array, so spawnFood, the collision checks (five near-identical loops), the reset block and the key handler all duplicate the same logic per snake; moveSnake special-cases `snake === snake1` to pick a DOM element; lightenColor's R/B/G variables are mislabelled (B holds green, G holds blue).

Core loop, growth, scoring and BFS search are correct, but several real flaws: spawnFood is called before the new head is unshifted, so food can be placed on the cell the head is about to occupy and becomes uneatable until the snake returns; head-swap collisions are missed (heads 1 apart trade cells and pass through each other, only caught incidentally by the body check); collisions are evaluated snake1-first, so identical situations are resolved asymmetrically; the CPU marks its own moving tail as a permanent obstacle and its fallback move has no lookahead, so it walks into dead ends; and the mirrored starting positions make a head-on crash the default outcome.

The grid, movement, growth, collisions, scores, CPU pathfinding, three modes, menus, and keyboard controls are present, but the R key only restarts after game over and does nothing during active gameplay.
The game runs and progresses without console errors, but the tested active-game R restart is inert.
The centered layout, restrained color scheme, readable overlays, and subtle grid produce a clean and polished presentation.

Core logic works, but active-game restart is blocked, crossing heads are resolved asymmetrically as a body collision, and food can rarely respawn on the eating snake's new head because spawning occurs before that head is inserted.

All named features exist in code (30x30 grid, growth, wall/self collision, WASD+arrow controls, BFS CPU, three modes, start menu, game over, 'R' restart), but the scoreboard is positioned at top:10px of a 904px-tall container that is vertically centered in a 100vh body with overflow:hidden, so at 1280x800 it is clipped off-screen — the score is not visible in any screenshot during gameplay, so 'display the score during gameplay' is not actually delivered. The 'CPU vs Human' mode also makes snake2 (P2/blue) the CPU while P1 stays human, contradicting its own label ordering.

No console errors and the simulation does run and progress, but the game is unplayable: both snakes spawn on the same row (snake1 head x=5 moving right, snake2 head x=14 moving left) 8 cells apart, so at ~120ms/tick they meet and both die after 5 ticks (~0.6s). interact-2 confirms 'GAME OVER / Draw!' after the click plus key presses — every session in every mode ends in a draw within a second unless the player reacts in under half a second. interact-3 ('R' to restart) is visually identical to the game-over state, so the restart keypress produced no observable effect. The board is also clipped top and bottom by overflow:hidden at 1280x800.

The menu and game-over screens are tidy and legible (green SNAKE title, styled buttons, red GAME OVER), but the 900px canvas inside a 100vh overflow:hidden body is cut off at both top and bottom, the scoreboard is clipped out of view entirely, and the menu panel's rgba(0,0,0,0.85) card is invisible against the black canvas so it reads as floating text. Playfield rows are hidden from the player.

Readable and commented, but with rough edges: GRID_SIZE (pixel size) vs TILE_COUNT (grid dimension) both equal 30 and are easy to confuse, an unfinished placeholder comment remains in drawSnake ('Simple logic to place eyes based on direction could go here // For now, just center dot'), BFS rebuilds the whole path array with [...path, ...] for every enqueued node, and spawnFood loops over both bodies without early exit.

Sensibly sectioned with clear function names, but snake1/snake2 are two copy-pasted object literals with duplicated init code instead of a factory, the two keydown switch blocks are near-identical duplicates differing only in key names and snake, and the mode dispatch in gameLoop nests a redundant 'cpu-human'/'cpu' check inside an outer test for the same two values.

Core mechanics (movement, growth, wall/self collision, BFS pathfinding with obstacle set and a shuffled survival fallback) read correctly, but the spawn layout is a design bug that makes a head-on mutual kill inevitable in about 0.6s. Head-to-head detection only compares equal cells, so two snakes swapping cells pass through each other undetected (it happens to be caught by the body check, but only by luck). If both heads land on the food in the same tick both score and spawnFood is called twice. The CPU obstacle map treats tails as permanent blockers, making the BFS more conservative than necessary.
Most requested features are implemented, but the 900px canvas is vertically clipped in the 800px viewport, placing the score board off-screen during gameplay.

The page runs without console errors and the menu works, but the snakes start facing each other on the same row and collide within roughly 0.6 seconds unless redirected immediately; the interaction evidence consequently reaches Game Over almost at once.

Core movement, growth, collision, controls, and BFS behavior are implemented, but the default placement creates an almost immediate collision, and the CPU search treats static bodies as obstacles without accounting for moving tails or simultaneous opponent movement.

All requested features present: 30x30 grid (TILE_COUNT=30), continuous movement, growth on food, wall/self collision ending the game, WASD/arrow keyboard controls, BFS-based CPU snake, all three modes (human vs human, cpu vs human, cpu vs cpu), live score board, start menu, game over screen with winner, and 'R' to restart.

console-errors.json is empty; menu buttons start the game (interact-1), arrow keys steer P2 and the simulation advances to a real game-over state (interact-2), and restart works. Only cosmetic wart: the initial draw() renders a stray food tile at (0,0) before spawnFood(), visible as a yellow square behind the menu.

Clean but plain: dark theme with a glowing title and consistent button styling, yet the playfield is a bare 600px black square with mostly empty space, the menu sits inside the canvas frame leaving large dead areas above and below, snakes are undifferentiated flat squares with no head marker, and a stray yellow food tile bleeds through the menu overlay at the top-left corner.

Contains leftover stream-of-consciousness reasoning committed as comments ('Wait, Mode 2 is CPU vs Human. Usually P1 is CPU? Let's assume...'), dead code (`if (!validMove) { // Do nothing, let it crash }`), an unused GRID_SIZE constant, unused CSS variables (--p1-color etc. duplicated as hardcoded hex in JS), and `validMove` assigned a boolean instead of the move it is named for.

Functions are reasonably named and separated, but the two snakes are never abstracted into a collection, so nearly every routine (init, collision, drawing, food-spawn validity) duplicates identical blocks for snake1 and snake2. Input handling has a redundant outer `if (gameMode === 1 || gameMode === 2)` wrapping a lone `if (gameMode === 1)`, and there is unreachable/no-op branching in cpuMove.

Core rules are right, but there are real flaws: snake1 and snake2 are moved sequentially against a shared food, so if snake1 eats, spawnFood() runs mid-tick and snake2 is then tested against the brand-new food in the same frame; isValidMove/BFS treat both snakes' tails as permanent walls and ignore that the path is recomputed every tick, so the CPU boxes itself in; the grid render loop stops at i < TILE_COUNT so the final right/bottom gridlines are missing; and the game ends the moment either snake dies, with no handling of simultaneous food consumption.

Menu, three modes, score board, game-over screen, keyboard controls and a BFS CPU are all present, but the core spec is missed: the board is 20x20, not 30x30 (`TILE_COUNT = 20`; `GRID_SIZE = 30` is the pixel size of a cell, not the grid dimension). There is also no single-player classic Snake - every mode forces two snakes, so 'human vs human' is the only shape available and there is no plain solo play.

No console errors, and the buttons respond, but the game is unplayable. Both snakes spawn on the same row facing each other (snake1 at x=5 heading +x, snake2 at x=14 heading -x) with only 9 cells between them, so at 100ms/tick they collide within ~5 frames. interact-1.png (immediately after clicking 'Human vs Human') already shows GAME OVER / DRAW! 0-0, and interact-2.png and interact-3.png show the identical instant draw. The player never gets to move; the same head-on spawn applies to all three modes.

Clean, legible dark menu with readable buttons and a centered board, but it is plain default styling - flat grey buttons, no polish on the board, and the game-over overlay leaves a stray coloured block behind 'P1 Score: 0' where snake bodies show through the translucent overlay.

Readable but sloppy: `GRID_SIZE`/`TILE_COUNT` are named backwards from their meaning (GRID_SIZE is a pixel size), the `keys` object and `handleKeyUp` handler are dead code that is written to and never read, and `lightenColor` names its channels R/B/G in a scrambled order. The menu hint says 'Restart: Enter' while the game is only restartable via a global keydown that calls `startGame(currentMode)` - pressing Enter on the fresh menu starts a game with `currentMode === ''`, which has neither human controls nor CPU.

Everything is duplicated per snake instead of looped over an array: wall checks, self-collision loops, cross-collision loops and direction updates are all written twice verbatim in `checkCollisions`, and `spawnFood` repeats the same body scan for each snake. Mixed with the dead input-state code, the result is mediocre rather than clean.

The spawn geometry makes the game end on its own within half a second in every mode - a fatal logic error, confirmed by all three interaction shots. Beyond that: the grid is 20x20 instead of the required 30x30; `moveSnake` is called for both snakes and food is consumed in snake1-then-snake2 order so snake2 can be tested against a food item snake1 just respawned; the BFS treats the snake body as permanently blocking (ignores the tail vacating) and copies the whole path into the queue on every push; when BFS returns empty the CPU's fallback picks the first valid neighbour without checking it is not a reversal; and when BFS's next step *is* a reversal the CPU silently keeps its old direction even if that drives it into a wall.

The artifact includes the menu, scores, game-over screen, controls, food growth, CPU pathfinding, and three mode buttons, but the board is 20x20 rather than the required 30x30, and CPU-vs-human is miswired: snake1 is simultaneously assigned CPU logic and human controls while snake2 has neither.

It loads without console errors, but Human vs Human predictably ends in a draw within about half a second because the snakes start facing each other and collide before normal play can develop. The R interaction also does not implement restart; only Enter does.
The implementation is readable and reasonably modular, but important configuration and mode-control mistakes remain, along with unused key-state tracking and misleading comments.

Core logic is materially broken: TILE_COUNT is 20 despite the 30x30 requirement, the default human match deterministically self-terminates almost immediately due to starting trajectories, and CPU-vs-human does not assign one functioning human snake and one functioning CPU snake.

All prompt requirements are present: 30x30 grid (GRID_SIZE=30 on a 600px canvas), continuous movement via setInterval, growth on food, wall/self collision ending the game, WASD + arrow keyboard controls, BFS-based CPU search for food, all three modes (Human vs Human, CPU vs Human, CPU vs CPU), live score board, start menu, game over screen with winner text, and restart via R keypress.

console-errors.json is empty; the start menu renders, the 'Human vs Human' button starts the game (interact-1), the simulation visibly progresses and reaches a correct GAME OVER screen with 'It's a Draw!' after arrow input and ~4.5s (interact-2), and interact-3 shows the snakes advanced from their spawn positions. The three timed shots are identical only because the start menu is static, which is expected.

Clean but plain dark theme: centered card, readable buttons, subtle canvas grid, glowing food. Defects: the GAME OVER heading inherits the green h1 color instead of a loss/neutral color, the P1/P2 score board sits visibly on top of the menu overlay before the game starts, and the page is a single small box on a large empty background with no other visual detail.

Ships an empty leftover `if (gameMode === 0 || gameMode === 2) { }` block (lines 400-405) containing the model's own self-dialogue comments ('Wait, logic check:', 'Actually, let's map controls...') — unfinished reasoning left in the artifact. Also a stray 'Visual feedback for selection could be added here' TODO, a `.btn.selected` CSS rule that is never applied, and a redundant `ctx.fillStyle = snake.color` before the loop that immediately overwrites it.

Reasonable function decomposition and naming overall, but snake1/snake2 are two hand-duplicated object literals with duplicated reset blocks instead of a factory, checkCollisions duplicates the same three-check sequence per snake, the explicit head-to-head block is dead code (checkEnemyCollision already iterates the enemy head), and lightenColor names its channels wrong (B holds green, G holds blue).

Core movement, growth, wall/self/enemy collision and BFS pathing are sound, but there are real flaws: checkCollisions unconditionally assigns snake1.dead = s1Dead, so an already-dead snake guarded by `if (!snake.dead)` gets its dead flag reset to false (masked only because endGame stops the loop immediately). The CPU obstacle set includes its own tail cell, which will have vacated by the next tick, so it needlessly rejects valid paths. The no-path fallback just takes the first non-blocked neighbor with no space/flood-fill check, so the CPU traps itself easily. spawnFood can loop forever on a full board, and the CPU assigns nextDirection directly, bypassing the reversal guard.
The artifact implements the 30x30 Snake game, three requested modes, CPU food search, keyboard controls, scoring, menus, game-over handling, and keypress restart.
The game starts, runs, and reaches game over without console errors, but the R restart key is ignored during active gameplay, as exercised by interact-3; it only works after GAMEOVER.
The centered board, restrained neon palette, clear grid, readable menus, and consistent controls styling form a polished presentation.
The implementation is readable, self-contained, and uses sensible helper functions for gameplay, AI, collision detection, and rendering.
The overall organization is reasonable, but handleInput contains an empty conditional and contradictory unfinished commentary, while unused selected-button styling also remains.

Core movement, growth, scoring, collision, and mode logic are functional, but restart handling is unnecessarily restricted to GAMEOVER and the CPU treats vacating tail cells as permanent BFS obstacles, potentially rejecting valid food paths.

30x30 grid, continuous movement, growth on food, wall/self collision, keyboard controls (WASD + arrows), BFS CPU snake, all three modes, live score, start menu, game over screen and R-to-restart are all present in the artifact.

No console errors in the tested path and the Human vs Human button and R key work, but the game is barely playable: both snakes spawn on row 15 facing each other 19 tiles apart at 80ms/frame, so with no input they collide head-on in ~0.8s - interact-2.png shows GAME OVER / Draw / 0-0 before the arrow keys could take effect. Additionally findPathBFS calls key(start) on line 375 before the const key arrow function is initialized on line 378, a TDZ ReferenceError that fires on the first CPU tick, so 'CPU vs Human' and 'CPU vs CPU' throw immediately and never run (untested by the interaction steps, hence the empty console log).

Clean dark neon theme with glowing title, consistent button styling and colored scoreboard, but the 900px canvas is taller than the 100vh body with overflow:hidden, so the bottom ~50px of the play field is clipped and unreachable; the game-over overlay is centered on the clipped area and its text overlaps the drawn snake segments (interact-2.png).

Readable, sectioned and commented, but contains a use-before-initialization bug in findPathBFS, leftover thinking-out-loud comments ('Prefer moves that keep distance...? Simple random valid move for now', 'Head is slightly larger or different shade?'), a potentially unbounded while loop in spawnFood, and redundant wall checks in both getNeighbors and isObstacle.

Two near-identical snake object literals instead of a factory, and the update/draw code duplicates every block per snake (self-collision loops, head-to-body loops, food handling branches, draw loops) rather than iterating over the two snakes; colors are also duplicated between CSS variables and JS literals.

Core movement, growth, wall/self collision and turn-reversal guards are correct, but the CPU path is dead code at runtime due to the TDZ error in findPathBFS, the fixed head-on spawn makes an unattended match end in a draw within a second, self-collision iterates the whole body including the tail that is about to move (false death) while isObstacle deliberately excludes it - an inconsistency between AI and collision rules, and food eaten by both snakes respawns without either snake keeping a consistent grow/pop invariant across the shared-food branch.

The single-file game includes the 30x30 board, menus, scores, two snakes, and three mode buttons, but both CPU modes crash, ArrowDown handling is incorrect, food makes both snakes grow, and R returns to the menu instead of directly restarting.

Human-vs-human starts and runs without captured load errors, but CPU play throws a ReferenceError because findPathBFS calls key before its const initialization. The P2 ArrowDown control is also faulty.
The presentation is coherent and readable, but visually basic; the fixed 900px canvas is clipped in the 1280x800 viewport, hiding the gameplay scoreboard.

The code is readable but contains several preventable implementation defects, including the temporal-dead-zone CPU crash, incorrect ArrowDown condition, shared growth behavior, and overly strict tail collision checks.
The script has clear naming, logical sections, and reasonably focused functions despite some duplicated two-snake handling.

Core logic is broken: every CPU-controlled mode fails immediately due to key being used before initialization, one movement control is incorrect, either snake eating causes both snakes to retain their tails, and collision checks incorrectly treat vacating tails as occupied.

All requested items are nominally present (30x30 grid, three mode buttons, start menu, game-over screen, R-restart, keyboard controls), but two requirements are not actually delivered: the CPU snake never searches for food (its BFS result is written to nextDx/nextDy which is never copied to dx/dy for CPU snakes, so it drives straight ahead into the wall), and the score board, though implemented, sits at top:10px of a 900px container that is clipped by the 800px viewport with body{overflow:hidden}, so no score is visible during gameplay in any shot.

No console errors and the buttons/keys respond (interact-1 starts the game, interact-3 restarts, interact-2 shows movement then a game-over screen), but the behaviour is buggy: the two snakes start on the same row heading at each other so a human-vs-human game ends within ~1-2s, the result is reported as 'Draw!' even though only one snake crashed, CPU modes end almost immediately because the CPU never turns, and the score display is off-screen.

The neon-on-black menu is tidy and legible, but the 900x900 container exceeds the 800px viewport with overflow hidden, so the board's top and bottom rows and its border are cut off and the score bar is entirely invisible; the play field is just a nearly-black grid with no visible walls or HUD.

Readable and commented, but contains a fatal oversight: the whole BFS/getSafeMove CPU section is effectively dead code because its output (nextDx/nextDy) is never applied for CPU snakes. Winner is passed to endGame() only in the head-to-head branch, so the wall/self-collision path always yields 'Draw!'.

Decent function decomposition and naming overall, but snake objects are declared once as globals then fully re-declared in startGame (duplicated literals), obstacle-building and direction arrays are duplicated between bfs() and getSafeMove(), GRID_SIZE actually means pixel size while TILE_COUNT means grid size (misleading names), and the 'r' restart is handled twice in handleInput.

Core human loop is sound, but several real defects: CPU direction is computed and then discarded (dx/dy never updated), so CPU snakes cannot chase food; collision is checked after unshifting the head but before checkFood pops the tail, so moving into the tail cell that is about to vacate is a false self-collision; and endGame() is called without a winner for all wall/self collisions, so the game always announces 'Draw!' regardless of who died.

Most requested features are present, but CPU snakes do not follow their computed paths: cpuMove updates nextDx/nextDy while moveSnake continues using unchanged dx/dy. The gameplay score is also clipped above the 1280x800 viewport.
The page runs without console errors, and human controls and restart work, but the CPU modes are functionally defective because CPU direction changes are never applied.
The retro neon presentation is coherent and readable, though the fixed 900px board exceeds the viewport and hides the scoreboard during gameplay.

The implementation is readable, but it contains significant behavioral mistakes, including unused CPU direction updates, incorrect draw outcomes for ordinary collisions, and unreachable special head-to-head handling.
The code is divided into clearly named input, game-loop, collision, rendering, and pathfinding functions with little duplication.

Human movement, growth, walls, and basic collisions work, but CPU snakes never adopt BFS-selected directions. All normal human-mode deaths call endGame without a winner and therefore report a draw, and collision checks can reject movement into a tail that would depart that tick.

Menu, three mode buttons, scoreboard, game-over screen, BFS CPU logic and a 30x30 grid all exist in the source, but the mode wiring is wrong: initGame always spawns 4 snakes and only sets CPU flags for P1/P2, so P3/P4 are always human in every mode, and 'human vs human' gives both human snakes the same shared key handler (no separate WASD/arrow players). The mode buttons also call a function that does not exist, so none of the required gameplay is actually reachable.

The buttons call startGame() but only initGame() is defined; console-errors.json shows three 'ReferenceError: startGame is not defined'. interact-1/2/3 are identical to shot-1 apart from button hover — clicking 'Human vs Human', pressing arrows, and pressing R all leave the start menu on screen. The game never runs.

Clean dark theme with readable buttons, but the overlay content is left-aligned inside the canvas box instead of centered, leaving a large empty area below, and the only rendered game content is a stray food dot in the top-left corner. No gameplay visuals are ever shown.

Readable and commented, but ships a fatal undefined-function reference in the HTML entry points, plus unused state (isPaused, gameMode), redundant dead branches in showGameOver (three status assignments overwritten), and no test of its own wiring.

Reasonable sectioning and a Snake class, but the button handlers do not match the function names, obstacle logic is duplicated between aiMove and bfs, safeMoves in aiMove is computed and then largely discarded, and showGameOver contains dead conditional branches.

Beyond the missing startGame entry point: bfs compares `s.id !== selfBody[0].id` where selfBody[0] is a coordinate with no id, so the caller's own body is never excluded correctly and all other snakes are always treated as obstacles including itself's owner mismatch; bfs returns null when the food is adjacent (path.length === 1 at target is impossible but the start-equals-target case returns null), and when the head is one step from food the returned direction is fine yet the fallback path picks a random move. handleInput applies one key set to every human snake so two humans cannot play independently, and CPU flags never reach P3/P4 despite four snakes spawning in all modes.

The artifact includes a 30x30 canvas, menus, scoring, collision/growth code, and the three requested mode buttons, but no startGame function exists, the CPU pathfinding is nonfunctional, and all human snakes share the same controls.
Every mode button throws ReferenceError: startGame is not defined. Interaction screenshots remain on the start menu, so gameplay cannot begin.
The code is readable and reasonably named, but it contains a missing public entry point and several major unfinished or incorrect gameplay paths.

Classes and functions provide some organization, but the undefined startGame handler, unused pause/player variables, hard-coded four-player setup, and confused BFS interface make the structure incomplete.

The game cannot start. Additionally, bfs returns an object while aiMove tests path.length, computes its direction relative to the target instead of the start, incorrectly identifies the current snake via selfBody[0].id, and human controls apply identically to every non-CPU snake.

All requested features are present: 30x30 grid (GRID_COUNT=30, 600px canvas / 20px tiles), continuous movement, growth on food, wall and self collision death, WASD + arrow keyboard controls, a BFS-based CPU snake, all three modes (pvp / cpu_vs_human / cpu_vs_cpu), live score board, start menu, game over screen with winner text, and restart on any keypress.

console-errors.json contains 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading draw)' captured before any interaction: the trailing draw() call at line 583 runs while snake1/snake2 are still undefined, so the initial canvas render aborts halfway (grid and food drawn, snakes never). The same handler bug means any keypress on the start menu also throws (keydown reads snake1.isCpu before initGame). Rubric caps this at 0 for runtime errors before interaction. Gameplay itself does run after clicking a mode, but pvp is nearly unplayable: snake1 spawns at y=5 heading up and hits the top wall in ~0.5s, which is exactly what interact-2 and interact-3 show — 'GAME OVER / Player 2 Wins!' with score 0 in both.

Clean, coherent dark theme with decent typography, colored per-player scores and key hints, but it is a single plain centered box with nothing else on the page, and the crashed initial render leaves the board empty behind the menu with a stray dark food dot bleeding through the translucent overlay (also visible as ghost snake segments over the GAME OVER screen).

Generally readable and commented, but has an unused `keys = {}` input object (dead code), the CPU flag is set twice — once via constructor argument and again by a redundant if/else chain in initGame that immediately overrides it — and the module-level draw() call is left in a position where it is guaranteed to throw.

Sectioned and mostly sensibly named, but with clear duplication: the direction array literal is repeated in getValidMoves and bfs, the occupied/obstacle Set is built identically in both, the `gameMode === 'pvp' || gameMode === 'cpu_vs_human'` guard is duplicated for each player block, and dead state (`keys`) plus the redundant isCpu reassignment block remain.

Core snake mechanics (movement, growth, wall/self/opponent collision, BFS pathing) are correct, but several real flaws: initial draw() dereferences undefined snakes; keydown dereferences snake1 before a game starts; self-collision tests the whole body including the tail cell that is about to vacate, so a snake dies when legally following its own tail; bfs treats the opponent tail as a permanent obstacle and its first step may be a 180° turn that setDirection silently rejects, leaving the CPU driving straight into a wall; placeFood loops forever if the board fills; and spawn positions/direction send snake1 into the top wall within 5 ticks.

scores.rationale: Menu, three modes, two-player controls, CPU BFS, score panel and game-over screen are all present, but the core 'grows when eating food' requirement is entirely absent: there is no head-vs-food check anywhere, so the snake never grows, the score never increments (updateScoreBoard is only called once at startGame) and food is never respawned after placeFood() at start.

No console errors and the page renders and animates (interact-1 shows a live board), but the game is not playable: both snakes spawn on row 15 facing each other and collide into each other's bodies within ~1s, so interact-2 and interact-3 both show the page already back at the start menu after only a few key presses. Clean, consistent dark arcade theme with readable typography, outlined buttons with hover states, subtle grid, glowing food and snake eyes; nothing broken, but also nothing beyond a competent standard layout.

Readable and commented, but unfinished: the eat/grow/score branch is simply missing, `isPaused` is declared and never used, draw() contains an if/else whose two branches are identical, and a stale comment in bfs() describes tail handling that was never implemented.

Reasonable function decomposition, but notable duplication: the two player objects and their reset lines are copy-pasted one-liners, the P1 and P2 key switch blocks are near-identical, the head-to-body collision checks are written twice, and magic pixel offsets for eyes are hardcoded.

Core game logic is broken. (1) No food-collision handling at all — no growth, no score, no food respawn. (2) CPU AI deadlocks: once its head reaches the food, bfs() returns a path whose first element is the head itself, so nextDx/nextDy become 0/0 and the CPU snake stops moving permanently. (3) In 'pvp' mode Player 1's switch also matches ArrowLeft/Up/Right/Down, so the arrow keys steer both snakes at once, making human-vs-human impossible. (4) Both snakes start on the same row moving toward each other with no input, guaranteeing a draw within ~10 ticks; head-to-head passing (they swap cells at non-integer crossing) is also not detected. (5) The 180-degree guard compares against the already-applied dx/dy rather than the queued nextDx/nextDy, so two fast presses in one tick can reverse the snake into itself.

The 30x30 board, menus, three mode buttons, controls, collisions, and score display exist, but food is never detected or eaten, snakes cannot grow or score, and CPU pathfinding selects the current head cell as its next step so CPU snakes remain stationary.

The page loads without console errors and Human vs Human starts, but core gameplay is defective: scoring/growth never occurs, CPU modes cannot move toward food, and Arrow keys also control Player 1 despite being documented for Player 2.
The code is readable and reasonably organized, but it is functionally unfinished: there is no food-consumption routine, and the BFS result is consumed incorrectly.

Core required logic is broken. No code checks either snake against food, increments tail or score, updates the scoreboard after eating, or relocates food. Additionally, bfs() returns a path beginning with the start node and cpuMove() uses path[0], setting CPU movement to (0,0) every tick.

Core logic is inverted and broken. updateCpuSnake starts with `if (!snake.isPlayer || !snake.alive) return;` but is only called for snakes where `!isPlayer` — so the AI body never executes and CPU snakes travel in a straight line into the wall. The update loop only moves snakes[0] when it is a player, so in 'ccp' (CPU vs CPU) snakes[0] never moves at all. Any single death sets isGameOver for everyone, so the game ends ~0.6s after start. Self-collision skips segments 0-3, letting short snakes pass through themselves; snake-vs-snake collisions are never checked at all; and the pause branch permanently kills the requestAnimationFrame chain.

updateCpuSnake immediately returns for every non-player snake even though it is only called for non-player snakes; the first CPU in CPU-vs-CPU is never updated; the supposed multi-human mode has no controls for a second human; pause stops scheduling frames permanently; and repeated starts can create concurrent animation loops.

Contains outright broken code: `const food = food;` (TDZ self-reference) inside CPU.decideDirection, `this.segments` referenced but never initialized, an undeclared global `opponent` used by the AI, three separate overlapping keydown listeners (the first one sets snake1 direction 'Up' for any arrow/WASD key), a `controls` object passed to every Snake and never read, and instructions describing Enter-to-restart that is not implemented.

Classes (Snake, Food, CPU) and draw/update/endGame sections give a readable skeleton, but there is substantial duplication and dead code: three keydown handlers doing overlapping work, a duplicated 8-branch switch, unused `controls`/`moveTimer` fields, both a phantom `segments` array and a derived `getSegments()` that contradict each other, and an unnecessary `gameLoopCallback` wrapper.

Core logic is broken. Self-collision uses `... && this.nextDirection.x !== 0 || this.nextDirection.y !== 0`, whose precedence makes it kill the snake on nearly any move, and it iterates the nonexistent `this.segments`. The snake body is derived from score via getSegments(), so a fresh snake has zero segments and is invisible; grow() pushes onto the nonexistent array. setNextDirection rejects valid turns when moving purely horizontally into a vertical move only via a convoluted condition. The CPU maximizes distance to food (`score = distToFood - ...`, picking the highest) instead of minimizing it, and crashes on the `food`/`opponent` references. Player 2 has no working controls in human-human mode (only uppercase W/A/S/D, and the earlier listener hijacks the event).

Readable and commented, but contains substantial dead/no-op code: the whole cpuMove function is unused; the 180-degree-turn guard in update() (lines 374-385) compares currentDir1 against nextDirection1, which is the same object reference, so it can never trigger; gameLoopFunction is a pointless wrapper around update(); direction1/direction2 are assigned but never read; the three branches in startGame are byte-identical; gameOver() calls checkGameOver() twice and interpolates its return into `Player ${'Player 2'} ...`, producing 'Player Player 2 hit the other player!'; the game-over message uses \n in textContent, which will not render as line breaks in HTML.

Flat globals with no encapsulation, and heavy duplication: the Player 2 keyboard block duplicates the Player 1 switch verbatim with the same keys (so both snakes react to the same arrows/WASD — confirmed in interact-2 where both moved down together), and is then followed by a third switch that again maps ArrowUp/Left/Down/Right onto Player 2. Dead code (cpuMove, direction1/direction2, gameLoopFunction) and the identical mode branches in startGame further muddy the structure.

Core rules are wrong. moveSnake returns null on wall or self collision but update() ignores the return value, so hitting a wall or itself just freezes that snake forever instead of ending the game — the central requirement is absent. Player 1's spawn geometry makes it self-collide on tick one, so it never moves. checkGameOver only detects head-into-other-snake, and because heads are compared against arrays that include the head itself it would also mis-fire in some cases. Food eaten by snake2 credits scores.p1. The anti-reversal guard is a no-op, so a direct 180 is possible. The CPU search is never wired into the loop.

Core flows are sound (ICS blob/download, validation, price math), but there are real flaws: revealOnScroll removes .active on scroll-out so content can disappear again; the initial reveal pass leaves everything below ~85% of the viewport permanently hidden until a scroll event fires; total price is formatted inconsistently ('€29' on open vs '€29.00' after quantity input); the email regex rejects valid TLDs longer than 4 characters; active-nav uses offsetTop without accounting for the sticky navbar; and the modals set aria-modal but implement no focus trap or focus restore.

console-errors.json is empty and the clicked controls respond (both Get Tickets buttons scroll to the tickets section, Save to Calendar shows its focus state and the Blob/download code is wired). The palette, serif hierarchy and glass panels are on-brief, but shot-full.png shows several concrete defects: all 8 artist images are broken placeholders showing alt text (source.unsplash.com returns nothing), and the hero background image likewise fails so the hero is an almost empty gradient band that does not reach the viewport edges; the FAQ block is six featureless gold rectangles with no visible text; tofu boxes appear in the hero metadata badge and in every ticket price; ticket feature bullets are drawn at `left:0` inside a 1.1rem padded list so the `•` overlaps the first letter of each line ('Ǝntry', 'Vain exhibition access'); and the timeline times sit at `left:-6.75rem`, pushing them to the far page edge, detached from the timeline rail.

Readable single IIFE with commented sections and sensible DOM APIs, but quality gaps: the palette is hardcoded as literal hex/rgba dozens of times instead of CSS custom properties, base `button` styling collides with `.faq-question` producing the invisible-text bug, an explicitly required feature (scroll reveal) is simply absent, and the source contains corrupted multi-byte characters that ship to the user as tofu.

Reasonably organised and mostly free of dead code, but the artist modal and ticket modal are two near-identical hand-rolled implementations (separate overlay CSS blocks, separate close/backdrop handlers, and two separate document-level `keydown` Escape listeners instead of one shared helper), and the outline/hover button treatment is copy-pasted across `.hero-buttons button`, `.artist-button` and `.select-tier-button` rather than sharing a class. FAQ state is also tracked redundantly in three places (`aria-expanded`, an `.active` class, and the `hidden` attribute).

Core flows (tier selection, price recalculation, form validation order, toast timeout, Blob download) read correctly, but the active-nav computation is wrong: `sections.findIndex(s => s.offsetTop > scrollPos) - 1` returns -1 at the top (clamped to 0, so 'Program' is highlighted while the hero is on screen) and returns -2 once the user scrolls past the last section (also clamped to 0), so the highlight jumps back to 'Program' at the bottom of the page instead of staying on 'FAQ'. The .ics DTSTAMP is malformed (trailing 'ZZ') and lines are LF-separated. The modals also have no focus trap and never restore focus to the triggering element on close, despite being labelled accessible.

The `.modal` class is referenced in HTML and JS but never defined in CSS — the central styling bug. Inline `style="..."` attributes are sprayed through markup (ticket lists, modal forms, venue copy) instead of using the existing class system. `$('#open-ticket-modal, .cta-btn, #nav-cta')` uses querySelector on a selector list, so only the first match gets the listener and the navbar CTA never opens the modal. String escaping bug in `join('\n')`. Name/email inputs in the ticket form have no id/name and are never read.

The 8 artist cards are hand-duplicated in HTML while the same names/images/bios are duplicated again in the `artistData` array — two sources of truth that already disagree (card images are 300x200, modal images 600x400). Three near-identical ticket-card blocks and six accordion blocks are copy-pasted. `#selected-price` is a hidden input used as state storage, `updateTotal` yields NaN when the modal is opened without a tier, and `<svg>{width:100%}` is a bare element selector that would hit any future SVG. Sections IDs and nav hrefs are out of sync (#program and #artists exist but are unlinked).

Several core flows are logically wrong. (1) `openModal` only sets display:flex; with no `.modal` positioning the dialog is not an overlay, so the checkout is unusable. (2) `$('#open-ticket-modal, .cta-btn, #nav-cta').addEventListener` binds one element only; the nav 'Get Tickets' instead hits the smooth-scroll handler bound to `.cta-btn`, which reads a null href and scrolls to #hero. (3) `join('\n')` emits literal backslash-n, so the downloaded .ics is invalid. (4) Opening the ticket modal from the hero leaves `#selected-price` empty, so `updateTotal` computes NaN and the tier heading is blank. (5) ESC hides modals but never resets aria-hidden; there is no backdrop-click close. (6) Scroll spy clears and re-adds `.active` inside a forEach over overlapping sections, so the last matching section wins rather than the current one.

scores.rationale: Massive under-delivery against the spec: only 2 ticket tiers instead of the 3 required (and named 'Museum Night Pass'/'VIP Experience' at PLN 250/450 instead of Night/Curator/Patron Pass at €29/€59/€129); only 4 artist cards instead of 8, with no 'View details' button; timeline has 5 invented slots instead of the 8 specified hours, and no location tags; FAQ has 4 questions instead of 6 and not one of the six required questions; navbar is missing the Tickets and FAQ links; venue section omits travel tips, accessibility notes and parking/public-transport notes, and the SVG map has no metro/bus marker, no entrance label and no gold route line; checkout modal has only an email field (no attendee name, ticket quantity, total price, terms checkbox or validation); footer omits the required 'Demo landing page — no real ticket purchase.' note and credits/social text links; none of the mandated Unsplash image URLs are used; the .ics uses the wrong filename (ARTIFACT_Museum_Night.ics) and wrong description/start-end encoding. Artist modal has no ESC close, no session time, and a Lorem ipsum bio.

console-errors.json is non-empty on plain load: five malformed `viewBox` attributes ('0 31 54', '0 29 45', '0 38 54', '0 53 69', '0 53 84') throw SVG parse errors, and the corresponding checkmark icons render broken in the ticket cards (visible in interact-1.png). The hero image is broken (alt text 'Museum Night Atmosphere' shown in shot-1/shot-3) and two of four artist images fail to load, leaving large black voids. In shot-full.png the FAQ and Newsletter sections render as an empty black band — their `.reveal` wrappers never get `.active`, so entire sections are invisible. The 'Save to Calendar' click produces an .ics whose DTSTART/DTEND ('202610181900Z', no 'T' separator, no seconds, TZID plus trailing Z) and DTSTAMP are invalid iCalendar and will not import.

Typography and the dark/gold palette are handled competently, but the full-page shot shows serious defects: the entire right half of the hero is a broken-image placeholder, the artist grid is mostly empty black with two broken images and one card floating alone, the SVG 'map' is run through `filter: invert(95%) sepia(20%)` producing a pale blue-grey box that clashes with the velvet theme, ticket checkmarks render as broken glyphs, and a tall empty black region sits where FAQ and Newsletter should be. Only two ticket cards leave the grid visibly unbalanced.

Inline `style="..."` attributes are used pervasively instead of the classes already defined; there is an invalid CSS declaration (`group;` inside `.artist-card`); five hand-written `viewBox` values are syntactically invalid; placeholder work is left in the shipped page (Lorem ipsum bio, `alert('Opening in maps...')`, `alert('Privacy Policy coming soon')`); an `sr-only` class is referenced but never defined; and a code comment openly concedes the artist modal image is a hard-coded fallback ('finding the img src ... is tricky without passing this').

Sections are ordered sensibly and CSS is grouped by area, but the accordion is driven by the fragile selector `div[style*="display: none"]` — querying elements by their inline style string — which breaks once the style is mutated. Dead/unused state exists (`currentTicketPrice`, `selected-ticket-name` hidden input never read), the artist cards duplicate identical markup with inline onclick handlers passing stringly-typed data instead of a data structure, and repeated inline style blocks duplicate what `.event-card`/`.ticket-features` classes already provide.

The flagship .ics generator is broken: `eventDate.toISOString().replace(...).split('T')[0]` plus `getHours()`/`getMinutes()` concatenation yields '202610181900Z' with no 'T' separator and no seconds, DTSTAMP is assembled from two mismatched slices, and TZID is combined with a trailing 'Z' — the file will not parse. `new Date('2026-10-18T02:00:00')` is compared/incremented in local time while the output is derived from UTC, so the end date can land on the wrong day. The accordion's 'close all others' only strips the `.active` class without resetting the previously opened panel's inline `display:block`, so old answers stay visible. The active-nav loop reads `#main-menu a` but the menu has no `#tickets`/`#faq` entries, so the state is wrong past the Venue section (interact-1.png shows 'Venue' underlined while sitting on Tickets). `openArtistModal` always injects the same hard-coded fallback image regardless of which artist was clicked. The checkout 'validation' is HTML `required` only — no name, quantity, total or terms logic exists.

scores.rationale: Large parts of the spec are missing or replaced with invented content. Timeline has 4 slots with invented times/titles instead of the 8 required (19:00–01:00), and no location tags. Only 3 artist cards instead of 8, with no role/teaser structure per spec, no 'View details' buttons, and no session time/bio in the modal. Ticket tiers are wrong entirely: Standard/VIP/Patron at $150/$350/$600 instead of Night Pass €29 / Curator Pass €59 / Patron Pass €129, and there is no 'recommended' badge. Checkout modal lacks selected-tier display, ticket quantity, total price and terms checkbox. FAQ has 4 invented questions instead of the 6 specified. Missing: meta description, the 3 concept feature cards, venue address/travel tips/accessibility/parking notes, SVG map metro-bus marker, entrance marker and gold route line, footer credits and the required 'Demo landing page — no real ticket purchase.' note. Nav links do not match (Concept instead of Tickets). None of the specified image URLs are used, and the .ics description/filename/end time differ from spec.

console-errors.json records 'TypeError: date.toISOString is not a function' — the Save to Calendar handler throws because endDate is `new Date(...).setHours(2)`, which returns a number, so no .ics file is ever downloaded (interact-2 shows nothing happening). The FAQ accordion is inert: each .accordion-body carries an inline `max-height:0` that the .active CSS rule never overrides (it only adds padding-bottom), so clicking a question never reveals an answer. Ticket selection fires a native alert() before opening the modal, and the selected tier is never written into the checkout. Hero background image and 2 of 3 artist images fail to load (visible alt-text placeholders in shot-full), so 'remote images load correctly' fails. The page does render and nav/modal/toast do work, so it is not fully broken.

Typography and palette are tasteful, but shot-full shows concrete visual defects: the hero has no image at all (pure black where the cinematic photo should be), two of three artist cards show broken-image boxes with raw alt text, and the entire newsletter + footer region at the bottom of the page is blank/invisible (reveal-on-scroll opacity never applied). Timeline bullet markers sit misaligned to the left of their rows, and the venue SVG label overflows the map container ('Re...' clipped at the right edge).

Single file with a reasonable order, but sloppy: invalid CSS property `group: hover` in .artist-card, a `.desktop-only` class used in markup but never defined, a `#checkout-tier-input` hidden field that is never populated or read, `<span class="nav-link" href="#">` (href on a span), the <footer> nested inside the newsletter <section>, a commented-out dead accordion block left in the JS, native alert() used in the purchase flow, and no ESC/backdrop close or focus management on modals despite 'accessible modal' being required.

Repetitive hand-written markup for every timeline slot, artist card and FAQ item rather than any data-driven or consistent pattern, heavy ad-hoc inline styles mixed with the stylesheet, hard-coded hex colors duplicating the CSS variables, dead commented-out code, unused selectors/ids, and a hard-coded section-name array in the scroll handler that omits the tickets section so its nav state can never activate.

Several concrete logic errors: `new Date("2026-10-18T02:00:00").setHours(2)` returns a timestamp number (and is the wrong day — the event ends 19 Oct 02:00), so formatDate throws and the .ics never generates; the accordion toggles an .active class that cannot beat the inline `max-height:0`, so answers never open; the tier/price read from data attributes is only shown in an alert() and never bound into the checkout modal or a total; the scroll spy iterates a fixed list excluding #tickets and #hero and uses element.offsetTop without accounting for section heights. Email validation, toast, modal open/close and reveal observer are otherwise correct.

Naming drifts between the spec's vocabulary and the implementation throughout.

The active-nav routine also writes inline styles rather than toggling the .active class it just removed, and it matches nav hrefs against every section including #hero and #tickets that have no corresponding link.

Presentation is tidy (section banners, small helpers, consistent naming), but the substance is poor: the lighting call is triplicated with identical arguments, the scanline fill is a per-pixel fillRect (worst possible Canvas 2D approach, and it shows in the FPS), the light 'position' is normalized and used as a global direction so it is really a directional light, and no comment or guard reflects that the shading is flat rather than per-vertex.

Organization and naming are reasonable, but there is real duplication and dead weight: c0/c1/c2 are three identical computations, drawTriangle destructures xa..bc (lines 124-126) and then never uses any of those bindings, mat3RotateZ/angleZ machinery is fine but the drawHalf(top,left,right) contract is so muddled that the first call passes pts[0] as both top and left, and the lerp helper takes a parameter named t that is actually an absolute y coordinate.

Multiple independent, fatal logic errors. (1) lerp computes f = t / dt where t is the absolute scanline y rather than (y - p1[1]), so every edge x/color interpolation is scaled by a meaningless factor - this is why the shapes are sheared slabs instead of triangles. (2) drawHalf(pts[0], pts[0], pts[1]) makes lp and rp identical (both lerp(pts[0], pts[1], y)), so xEnd <= xStart and the entire upper half of every triangle is skipped. (3) Backface culling is inverted: for the front face [0,1,2,3] at z=-1 the cross product yields normal z = +4, which the test 'if (normal[2] > 0) continue' discards, so the faces nearest the camera are culled and the far faces are drawn. (4) Per-vertex lighting uses the face normal for all three vertices, so no Gouraud interpolation exists at all.

No console errors and the animation clearly progresses across shot-1/2/3, but the output is functionally wrong out of the box: instead of a cube the canvas shows a few disconnected, partially erased triangles. Cause is visible in code - drawTriangle() builds an ImageData with alpha 0 outside the triangle and uses ctx.putImageData over the whole bounding box, which replaces (not blends) pixels, so each face's second triangle wipes the first and neighbouring faces wipe each other. putImageData also ignores the ctx.setTransform(dpr,...) scaling, so on a HiDPI viewport geometry is written at the wrong scale/offset. Several defects that break the effect. (1) drawTriangle writes an opaque-or-transparent ImageData over the triangle's whole bounding box with putImageData, so it erases previously drawn geometry instead of compositing - the two triangles of every quad destroy each other. (2) putImageData bypasses the dpr transform set in resize(), so pixel coordinates are inconsistent with the rest of the drawing. (3) The painter's-algorithm sort is inverted: z = p[2] + cameraZ grows with distance, and sorting ascending draws nearest triangles first so far geometry overpaints near geometry. (4) Per-vertex lighting reuses the single flat face normal, so it is not real Gouraud shading. Together these produce the broken, cube-less output seen in the shots.

Reasonable single-IIFE layout with small vector helpers, but naming and hygiene are sloppy: three dead declarations (faceNormals, shadeColor, shade), barycentric weights named w1/w2/w3 while pairing with c0/c1/c2 which invites off-by-one confusion, the `tris` array actually holds quads (4 indices in `pts`), and p0..p3 are recomputed/shadowed in both the build loop and the draw loop.

The face index lists have inconsistent winding, so cross(p1-p0, p2-p0) yields an outward normal for some faces (x=-1, z=+1) and an inward normal for others (x=+1, z=-1). The cull test dot(n,[0,0,1]) <= 0 therefore keeps back faces and discards front faces depending on which face it is, which produces the holes and missing faces in the screenshots; the sign is also inverted relative to the camera, which sits at z=-4.5 looking toward +z, so visible faces should have negative-z outward normals. The same wrongly-signed normal feeds the vertex normal (normalize(pos)+n), so lighting on those faces is wrong too. Reading the code, the pipeline is wrong in several independent places. (1) Color space: base colors are 0..1 but calculateLighting's output goes straight into ImageData bytes, so every pixel is 0 or 1 - guaranteed black regardless of lighting. (2) rasterizeTriangle's putImageData overwrites the whole bounding rect with alpha-0 pixels outside the triangle, destroying background and earlier triangles - a rasterizer cannot be built this way. (3) Painter's algorithm sorts ascending by avgZ (a.depth - b.depth) while the projection uses z+5 as the divisor, i.e. larger z is farther from the camera; so the farthest triangles are painted LAST, inverting the depth order. (4) Lighting and backface culling both use the face normal from the ROTATED quad but the light vector is computed in that same rotated space against a fixed world light, and culling tests normal.dot(0,0,-1) with no consistent winding guarantee across the six faces (e.g. [0,1,2,3] vs [4,7,6,5] vs [0,4,5,1]), so front and back faces are not reliably separated - visible as the incomplete, gap-ridden silhouette. (5) Gouraud interpolation is degenerate because all three vertex colors share one normal. Also the barycentric invDenom has no degenerate-triangle guard, so an edge-on triangle divides by ~0.

Multiple compounding errors break the pipeline. (1) Face winding is inconsistent: faces [0,1,2,3] (-z) and [0,3,7,4] (-x) produce inward normals under cross(v1-v0, v2-v0), so the averaged per-vertex normals are wrong - vertex 0 gets ~(0.58,-0.58,0.58) instead of pointing toward (-1,-1,-1). (2) Backface culling is inverted: a face pointing at the camera has fn_z<0, so dot(fn,[0,0,-1])>0 and it is culled, keeping the away-facing ones. (3) The rasterizer only fills when all three edge functions are >=0, so triangles of the opposite screen winding are silently dropped - together with (1) and (2) this is why whole faces are missing. (4) There is no z-buffer or depth sort, which is only safe with correct culling on a convex hull. (5) Pause zeroes the angles rather than freezing time. (6) The wireframe pass writes to the canvas before putImageData wipes it.

The rasterizer's winding convention is inverted relative to the culling test, so front faces are never filled. edge(a,b,c) returns the negation of the standard cross product, so for a triangle kept by the cull (camera-space normal.z < 0) combined with the y-flip in the viewport mapping (y: -projA.y*sy + sy), `area` comes out negative and every interior pixel yields w0,w1,w2 < 0, failing the `w0>=0 && w1>=0 && w2>=0` test. Nothing is drawn; only near-degenerate edge-on triangles whose winding flips under the per-vertex perspective divide leak through, which is exactly the slivers seen in the screenshots. Secondary flaws: backface culling uses a fixed (0,0,-1) view direction rather than the vector from the camera to the face, which is wrong for a perspective camera; vertex normals are face normals so the Gouraud interpolation degenerates; and there is no z-buffer or depth sort.

The pipeline is broken as written. (1) Missing model/projection scale means projected extents are sub-pixel, so the cube is invisible - the primary defect, visible in every shot. (2) The rasterizer accepts only w0,w1,w2 >= 0, i.e. a single winding, while the quad splits produce a mix relative to the screen-space area sign, so triangles that survive culling can still be skipped; area is used as a signed divisor without normalizing sign. (3) Backface culling uses the transformed (pre-projection) normal with a hardcoded n[2] >= 0 test rather than a view-direction dot product, which is inconsistent with the projection convention (y is flipped at projection time). (4) Painter's sort keys on average z but the perspective uses fov/(fov+z), so the far-to-near ordering direction is not verifiable as consistent. (5) Drawing via per-triangle getImageData means each triangle's readback includes previously drawn pixels; the alpha=255 writes also defeat the clearRect transparency assumption for overlapping bounds.

The core 3D math is wrong. The six face normals are constants in model space and are never passed through rotate(), while the vertices are rotated every frame — so the backface test (normal · camToFace) and the Lambert dot product both use normals that no longer match the geometry, which is exactly the missing-faces / near-flat shading seen in the shots. Projection maps x=±1 at z=4 to 0..width, so the cube always overflows the canvas. There is no z-buffer or painter's-algorithm sort, so face overlap is undefined. sceneBuffer is sized once at load and never rebuilt in resize(). The rasterizer also rejects w1/w2/w3 >= 0 without handling negative area (clockwise triangles get dropped).

All requested pieces are present: cube vertices, X/Y/Z rotation, perspective projection (400/z), backface culling, faces split into triangles, per-vertex Lambert lighting with barycentric color interpolation, a moving light (sin/cos orbit), W wireframe toggle, P pause and an FPS readout.

No console errors and the animation clearly progresses across shot-1/2/3 at ~60 FPS, but the render is visually wrong: backface culling keeps the wrong set of faces (kept when normal·[0,0,-1] < 0, i.e. faces pointing away from the camera), so the visible solid reads as an inside-out/concave box in shot-3 rather than a cube. Shading also does not follow the cube's rotation because vertex normals are never rotated.

Smooth gradient interpolation and a clean monospace HUD, but the silhouette is visibly broken/concave in shot-3 (open-box interior look), the palette is a single flat blue, the object is small on an otherwise empty page, and edges are hard-aliased with no anti-aliasing.

Readable and self-contained, but wasteful and partly dead: a full-screen ImageData is allocated and manually background-filled every frame (a ~4M-element loop) even in wireframe mode where it is never used; there is no z-buffer and no depth sorting, and drawTriangle re-derives barycentrics per pixel with divisions instead of incremental edge functions.

Sectioned and reasonably named (vec3 helpers, geometry, project/rotate/drawTriangle/loop), but the wireframe branch leaves the entire ImageData construction as dead work, face normals `n` are hand-authored and duplicated per triangle alongside a recomputed cross product, vec3.mulScalar is never used, and the rotate() function inlines three hardcoded matrices instead of a reusable matrix helper as the task asked.

Two real errors. (1) Backface culling is inverted: for the front face [0,1,2] the cross product yields +z, and the test `dot(normal,[0,0,-1]) >= 0 -> cull` therefore discards the camera-facing faces and keeps the far ones. (2) Lighting uses the static object-space `vertexNormals` against a world-space light direction while the vertices are rotated, so the shading does not rotate with the cube. Also `lightDir = normalize(lightPos)` treats the light as purely directional, ignoring vertex position, and there is no depth buffer so triangle overlap is resolved by draw order.

Lighting uses unrotated, model-space vertex normals and a normalized light position rather than a per-vertex vector from the moving light to each rotated vertex, so the Gouraud lighting is not physically correct as the cube rotates.

All named pieces appear in the source (rot matrices, perspective project(), backface cull, quad->triangle split, Lambert per-vertex, orbiting light, W/P handlers, FPS in HUD), but the central deliverable - a Gouraud-shaded rotating cube - is not delivered: the front face is defined as [4,6,5,4], so one of its two triangles is degenerate, and the rasterizer emits stretched slivers instead of a cube. Requirements are present on paper only, partially realized on screen.

console-errors.json is empty and the frame content clearly changes between shot-1, shot-2 and shot-3, so it runs and animates. But the output is wrong: no cube is ever visible, only huge triangles bleeding off all four canvas edges (shot-full.png), and the reported FPS is 2/11/13 for six triangles because the rasterizer does a per-pixel ctx.fillRect over spans that span the whole viewport. Logic bugs, not a clean run.

shot-full.png shows no recognizable cube - a few flat purple/blue/orange wedges stretching past the screen edges with black gaps between them. The subject of the effect never renders; this is a broken visual, not a merely weak one.

Reasonable section comments and small vector helpers, but littered with dead and broken code: lerpColor() and interpolate() are never called and interpolate() is itself wrong (b: c1.b - c1.b*t ignores c2 entirely); lightPos, add(), scale(), PI/TAU are unused; each face carries a `normal` field that is never read; the comment 'we use winding' contradicts the painter's sort right below it.

Single flat script with no module boundaries; matMul is defined after its only call site at the bottom of the file while every other helper is grouped at the top; transform() and edgeInfo() are re-declared as closures inside the per-frame loop; vertices are projected once in `projected` and then re-transformed a second time per triangle, duplicating the same work. Face labels are also wrong (the entry commented 'left' is the bottom face, 'bottom' is the left face).

The rasterizer is fundamentally broken. sortVertices(p0,p1,p2) swaps only its local parameter bindings, so it is a no-op for the caller - drawTriangle then relies on p1 being the middle vertex, which it is not, so the y<p1.y upper/lower split and both edge slopes are wrong, producing the screen-spanning wedges seen in every shot. The lower half sets rStart/rEnd (and g,b) to the identical c1->c2 expression, so there is no horizontal color interpolation there at all, and xEnd is taken from an edge parameterized off p0 while xStart comes off p1. Face [4,6,5,4] yields the degenerate triangle (4,5,4). Lighting uses one geometric faceNormal for all three vertices, so the 'per-vertex' variation comes only from the light vector. Backface culling compares against a fixed viewDir (0,0,-1) with no view-vector-per-face, and the hand-written face normals it might have used are wrong anyway.

Most required pieces appear in the source (rotation matrices, perspective projection, a culling test, quad->triangle split, Lambert per-vertex lighting, moving light, W/P handlers, FPS readout), but the central requirement - Gouraud-interpolated rasterized faces - is not actually delivered: nothing but 8 vertex dots is ever drawn on screen, and the 'interpolation' in drawTriGouraud only lerps between c1 and c2 along x, ignoring c3 and any vertical variation, so it is not true per-vertex color interpolation even in principle.

console-errors.json is empty and the FPS counter reads 60, but the cube itself never appears. shot-1/2/3 show only a radial-gradient background, the HUD, and a handful of 1-2px white dots (the projected vertices). The dots move between shots so the loop runs, yet no shaded or wireframe geometry is ever rendered - the primary deliverable does not work.

The file ships a ~100-line dead function drawFilledTriangle that is never called and contains an abandoned scanline loop whose body computes xLp/xRp and discards them, plus leftover self-narration comments ('Actually let me redo this properly with a clean scanline approach', 'Actually we need per-vertex color interpolation. Let me use barycentric coords.'). Other dead code: matMulVec3 as a pointless alias of mulMat3Vec3, unused rotZ, unused viewDir, unused avgNormal/avgLightDir/avgDiffuse, unused scale3/vec3 helpers, unused tTop/tBot. This reads as unfinished, uncleaned output.

Two competing rasterizer implementations (one entirely dead), duplicated lerpColor/lerp definitions, a stale in-function loop that duplicates the logic below it, inconsistent naming (rotY the matrix builder vs rotY_A the angle), and a large block of never-executed code left in the shipped file.

Multiple genuine logic errors. (1) In drawTriGouraud the edge walk does 'if(y<a[1]||y>b[1]) continue' without ordering a/b by y, so any edge whose second vertex is above its first is silently skipped; a triangle then yields fewer than 2 crossings and draws nothing at all - which matches the blank screenshots. (2) Scanline color uses only lerp(c1,c2,u) horizontally, so c3 is never used and there is no vertical gradient; this is not Gouraud shading. (3) Backface culling compares the cross-product normal against the vector to the origin using a sign that appears inverted for the given vertex winding, so visible faces are discarded. (4) Depth sort uses raw object-space z of transformed verts rather than camera-space depth. (5) fpsTimer accumulates the clamped dt, so reported FPS is biased whenever a frame exceeds the 0.05s cap. The net result is that the described pipeline never produces a cube.

The file nominally contains the requested pieces (vertex list, rotateX/Y/Z, perspective project(), a culling test, quad->triangle split, Lambert per-vertex intensity, moving light, W/P key handlers, FPS counter), but the central deliverable - a Gouraud-shaded rotating cube - is never produced on screen. Requirements are present as code only, not as working features, so at best partial.

The page renders nothing but the yellow light-glow sprite and the HUD; no cube is ever visible in shot-1, shot-3 or shot-full. Two fatal bugs guarantee this: fillTriangle() clears the z-buffer with zbuf.fill(-Infinity) and then does `if (z > zbuf[zi]) continue;`, so every fragment (z > -Infinity) is skipped and no pixel is ever written; and the backface test `dot(norm, normalize(fVerts[0])) < 0` culls with a bogus view vector. Even if a face survived culling, computeVertexNormal() returns a single vec3 but is indexed as `vNormals[tri.i0]`, yielding undefined and a TypeError inside dot(). The animation is alive (FPS 60, light dot moves between shots) yet the effect itself is entirely absent - it does not run as expected without fixes.
shot-full is a black page with a small blurred yellow dot and a 3-line green HUD. No cube, no shading, no wireframe - visually broken, nothing of the intended effect is on screen.

Unfinished and internally inconsistent. drawTriangle() is ~55 lines of dead code that references undeclared identifiers (ixStart, ixEnd2) and has variables (x3, dI2a interpolants) that are computed and thrown away; it is never called. A `projected` array is built in render(), computes a lightDir and a normal it discards, and is never used. vertexNormalsCache is declared and never touched. Per-face nDotL0/1/2 are computed then ignored in favour of the vNormals path. Comments claim behaviour the code does not implement ("will be recomputed per-face").

Two competing rasterizers (scanline drawTriangle and barycentric fillTriangle), one of which is dead; large blocks of unused computation; a hard-coded 1600x900 z-buffer stride that does not match the resizable canvas (indexing is done with ZBUF_W while bounds come from canvas.width, and no reallocation on resize); computeVertexNormal does an O(n) findIndex position lookup per triangle to recover an index the caller already has, then returns a single object where an indexable map is expected. Naming is muddled (b vs b_, i vs ix1/ir1, x3 unused). Duplication and dead code dominate.

The pipeline is broken at several independent points. (1) Z-test inverted relative to the clear value: buffer filled with -Infinity and fragments rejected when z > buffer, so all fragments are discarded. (2) Backface culling uses normalize(fVerts[0]) - the vector from the world origin to a vertex - as the view direction while the camera sits at z=-4 in project(); the test sign and the vector are both wrong, so visibility is arbitrary/inverted. (3) computeVertexNormal(vi, faceVerts) is passed a global cube index (0-7) but indexes faceVerts (length 4), so it reads undefined for most faces, and it returns one vec3 that the caller subscripts as vNormals[tri.i0] - always undefined. (4) The vertex normals it would compute are derived from untransformed model-space vertices while lightDir uses rotated positions, mixing coordinate spaces. (5) triData builds triangles from face.verts values used as indices into the per-face `proj` array, mixing global and local indexing again. The screenshots confirm the net result: nothing draws.

The face winding/culling test rejects every cube face. Additionally, triangle projection indexes face-local arrays with global vertex indices, and computeVertexNormal returns a vector but is treated as an indexed collection.

All required pieces are nominally present in the source (rotation matrices, perspective projection, backface culling, quad->triangle split, per-vertex Lambert shade, moving light, W/P handlers, FPS HUD), but none of it is delivered at runtime: the page throws on every frame and renders nothing, so wireframe toggle, pause, FPS display and Gouraud shading are all effectively missing. Also, the 'Gouraud' color interpolation is fake - all three triangle vertices are passed the identical face base color, and the scanline interpolates only between v0 and v2 colors, so there is no true per-vertex color gradient.

console-errors.json is full of 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading \'x\')' thrown every frame. Root cause: line 317 `const shades = wi.map(i => shade(wv[i], ...))` indexes the 4-element `wv` array with global vertex indices 0..7, so wv[i] is undefined for i>3 and vSub crashes. Result: shot-1/2/3 and shot-full are a uniform empty #0a0a1a viewport - no cube, not even the HUD text (the render function throws before writing the HUD). Nothing runs; W and P do nothing observable.
Every screenshot, including shot-full.png, is a completely blank dark-blue page. No cube, no wireframe, no HUD, no FPS readout - there is nothing to look at.

The file contains abandoned scaffolding left in place: line 177-180 builds `rgbs`, `orig` and an `idx` array the author annotates '// wrong approach' and then comments 'Let's redo properly', leaving the dead code in the shipped artifact. Line 297 computes `fn` via two redundant matrix rebuilds per face per frame, line 301 computes an 'average depth' from `wv0.z` plus the transformed origin (always 0), which is not an average depth at all. Line 353-358 computes s0/s1/s2 and then a second unused `si` mapping. Unfinished and unverified.

Sectioning and naming are reasonable (clear banner comments, small vector helpers), but there is real dead code (`orig`, `idx`, `rgbs`, `shades` shadow at line 176, unused `si`), duplicated wireframe drawing (a quad stroke immediately followed by the same four edges drawn again), an unused `hslToRgb`/`clamp` mix of concerns, and per-frame reconstruction of rotation matrices already computed in transformCube.

Multiple hard logic errors. (1) Fatal index bug at line 317: `wv[i]` indexed by global vertex ids 0..7 against a 4-element array - crashes every frame. (2) Backface culling at line 240 uses world/model-space vertices with a fixed viewDir (0,0,1) and ignores the perspective camera, so it is not correct culling; the rotated face normal `fn` is computed but never used for the test. (3) Painter's-algorithm depth key (line 301) is `(wv0.z + 0)/2` - a single vertex's z halved, not a face average, and sorted ascending which draws near faces first for this coordinate convention. (4) The rasterizer's color interpolation lerps only v0->v2 by the horizontal t, ignoring v1 entirely, and the left/right scanline edges are picked without ordering x, so spans can be inverted; the shading is therefore not real barycentric Gouraud. (5) All three triangle vertices receive the same base color, defeating the per-vertex interpolation the task asked for. (6) The 'shade' function silently adds a Blinn-Phong specular term with camDir treated as a fixed point rather than the camera position in the rotated frame.

scores.rationale: All requested pieces are nominally present (rotation matrices, perspective projection, culling, quad->triangle split, per-vertex Lambert, moving light, W/P keys, FPS), but the central deliverable - a Gouraud-shaded cube - is not achieved: the rasterizer drops entire triangles and the culling test keeps the wrong faces, so the render is a few disconnected polygons rather than a shaded cube, and no visible color gradient is produced.

No console errors and the animation does progress across shot-1/2/3, but the output is wrong out of the box: faces are missing (visible holes and a see-through interior in shot-full.png), the shape never reads as a cube, and the first second runs at FPS 1 because of per-pixel fillRect. Also a latent ReferenceError (`t2[5]` at line 237, `t2` is not in scope) will throw whenever a flat-top triangle hits that branch.

The scene is broken: instead of a cube there are two or three detached quads/triangles with large gaps, the geometry has no closed silhouette, and most frames are nearly black (shot-1 and shot-3 are barely visible). No perceptible Gouraud gradient across the faces. Only a HUD and background gradient look intentional.

Dead and broken code left in place: `drawSpan` is never called and would throw (`tBot.color` on a number), `face.normal` is declared for all six faces and never used, `xMid`/`xLeftTop`/`leftT` are computed and discarded, `tR` is computed twice in the same block, and line 237 references an undefined `t2`. The rasterizer is written as three copy-pasted inner loops instead of one.

Section banners and small vector helpers are reasonable, but `drawFilledTriangle` is ~135 lines of near-identical duplicated scanline blocks with cryptic names (cR/cG/cB vs cR2/cRR/cGG, p0[3..5] index-based color access), plus the dead function and unused face-normal data noted above. The wireframe branch re-derives the sibling triangle with an ad-hoc `(item.tri[0]===0 && item.tri[1]===2)` test and strokes each quad twice.

Multiple compounding errors. (1) Backface culling is inverted: for the front face (verts 0,1,2 at z=-S) cross(e1,e2) yields +z, and the test `dot(n,(0,0,-1)) < 0 -> continue` therefore culls camera-facing faces and keeps the far ones. (2) The scanline fill assumes the p0->p2 edge is always the left edge; there is no left/right swap, so whenever xLeft > xRight the `for (x=xLeft; x<=xRight)` loop body never executes and the whole triangle disappears - exactly the missing faces seen in the shots. (3) Horizontal color interpolation is reversed: the x-loop starts at xLeft (the p0->p2 edge) but seeds with `cR`/`cRR`, the opposite edge's color, and lerps toward `cR2`, so the gradient is mirrored. (4) Line 237 uses undefined `t2`, a latent crash. (5) All vertices of a face share the flat face normal, so 'per-vertex' lighting varies only by distance to the light, and the light intensity is never clamped to <=1.

The triangle rasterization logic produces incorrect geometry and interpolation, causing the cube faces to disappear or render as disconnected triangles; one reachable rasterizer branch also references undefined t2.

All the named pieces appear in the source (rotation matrices, perspective projection, a culling test, quad->triangle split, Lambert term, moving light, W/P handlers, FPS readout), but the core deliverable is not met: the geometry list contains the bottom and top faces twice and no +X/-X faces at all, so it is not a cube, and the per-pixel color interpolation is mis-derived, so no Gouraud gradient is produced. The screenshots confirm flat, uniform faces and a degenerate shape.

No console errors and the animation does progress between shot-1, shot-2 and shot-3, but the output is wrong: shot-1 shows an almost entirely black solid, shot-3 and shot-full show a single flat quad instead of a cube. The software rasterizer uses one ctx.fillRect per pixel, giving FPS 1 at 1s and 7 at 6s per its own HUD - unusable as a 'realtime' effect.
