The HUD and light glow are tidy, but the subject itself is broken: faces render near-black in the first seconds and later as one over-saturated flat blue quad with no shading gradient, no cube silhouette, and visible holes where the missing side faces should be.

Readable helpers and section comments, but a lot of abandoned work is left in: cr/cg/cb are computed with a nonsensical nested-lerp formula and immediately discarded, `area` is computed as e1x*e1y - e1y*e1x (always 0) and unused, an `if` block at the flip-normal step has an empty body with only a comment, and camDir/viewDir/add/scale are dead. A face is declared with a comment admitting 'wrong winding fixed below' and then mutated on the next line.

Sections and naming are reasonable, but there is duplication and dead code: the faces table repeats the top and bottom faces instead of defining left/right, a const face entry is patched by mutation after declaration, two full color-interpolation implementations sit side by side with one unused, and several unused vector helpers and locals remain.

Multiple independent logic breaks. (1) Barycentric weights use w1=c2v+c3v etc., which sum to 2*totalArea, so bw1+bw2+bw3 = 2 and each weight is the complement of the correct one - colors are doubled and inverted, destroying the Gouraud interpolation. (2) For the second triangle [i0,i2,i3] the per-vertex light directions and shades are still computed from indices[0..2], so colors are attached to the wrong vertices. (3) Backface culling dots a model-space normal (built from untransformed `vertices`) against a rotated position, mixing coordinate spaces, so culling is wrong and faces vanish. (4) Lighting is also done entirely in model space, so cube rotation does not change shading. (5) The face table omits both X faces and duplicates the top and bottom, so the mesh is not a closed cube. All of this is visible in the shots.

Unfinished draft quality: the file contains long stream-of-consciousness comment blocks debating with itself (lines 112-157, 302-306, 366-374), three stacked bodies of drawGouraudTriangle (two dead ones at 396 and 446, the second containing unreachable/duplicate const declarations of minY/verts that are themselves a redeclaration error), a placeholder getIntensity helper, undeclared globals (ambientIntensity, diffuseFactor, verts referenced inside 446), and a fatal syntax error. Two functions with the same name drawGouraudTriangle plus a third inlined body; abandoned `faces` array in createCube (lines 182-189) that is never used; getColor defined twice (a 2-arg local at line 350 and a global at 566) with conflicting signatures; Triangle stores an unused this.color and a getVertexNormal that just returns the face normal; dead branches in render (the identical if/else at 381-390). Duplication and dead code dominate the file.

Broken beyond the syntax error. Triangle's constructor assigns `this.v[0]` without ever creating `this.v`, a guaranteed TypeError. Backface culling dots a normal computed from untransformed model-space edges against a constant view vector, so culling never changes as the cube rotates. project() uses the outer `v` array instead of its `vtx` parameter (`v.x` on an array is undefined), producing NaN coordinates. Rotation increments angles by `dt * 0.5` / `dt * 1.2` in radians-per-millisecond, ~30 rad per frame — the cube would spin incoherently. Lighting mixes a light in unit-scale world coords (radius 3.5) with vertices at scale 100, so the light is effectively at the origin. Intensity is computed from the face normal for all three vertices, so no color varies across a face — flat, not Gouraud. The keydown handler appends to innerHTML instead of updating, so the HUD would accumulate duplicate lines.

Projection uses z_view = v.z + 5.5 with scale fov/z_view, so larger world z is farther from the camera; under that convention the visible faces are the ones with normals pointing toward -z, yet the screen-space cull keeps faces whose edge cross product is negative, which for the identity-rotation front quad [4,5,6,7] (outward normal +z, i.e. facing away) evaluates to -32041 and is kept while the true near face [0,3,2,1] is discarded. The renderer therefore consistently draws the back-facing set, producing the hollow/inverted cube and a shading result inconsistent with the drawn light marker. Also, 'per-vertex' normals are just the flat face normal, so interpolation only comes from the point light's varying direction, not from real vertex normals. The rest is sound: winding is consistent with the declared normals, the painter's sort (descending z = farthest first) is correct for this depth convention, and the incremental barycentric loop and degenerate-triangle guard are right.

Colors are also interpolated in screen space without perspective correction and there is no z-buffer, only per-face average-depth sorting.

The cube's face index lists are not consistently wound. cross(b-a, c-a) gives +Z for face [0,1,2,3] (which sits at z=-1, so outward is -Z), -X for [1,5,6,2] (at x=+1) and -Y for [3,2,6,7] (at y=+1) - three of six normals point inward. This corrupts the accumulated per-vertex normals (e.g. vertex 6 at (1,1,1) gets normal ~(-1,-1,1) instead of (1,1,1)), so the Lambert term is computed against wrong directions - hence the near-black faces. It also inverts the screen-space cull test for the correctly-wound half: the test keeps faces whose winding-normal points away from the camera, which is right for the three inverted faces and wrong for the other three, so for each opposite-face pair both faces are drawn half the time and both are culled the other half. That is exactly the hole-through-the-cube seen in every screenshot. Painter's-sort with no z-buffer only masks the double-draw case, not the missing-face case.

Two core pipeline steps are inverted. The face winding produces inward normals (e.g. face [0,1,2,3] at z=-1 yields cross = (0,0,+4) instead of (0,0,-1)), so `dot(normal, viewDir) < 0` culls the visible near faces and keeps the far ones. Additionally, per-vertex normals use normalize(vertexPosition) (spherical, not cube) and the light is normalized to a direction, so Lambert intensity is only loosely physical; the on-screen light marker uses a separate unrelated 2D formula.

judges.rationale: All 6 attempts take an identical approach: a two-snake competitive 'SNAKE BATTLE' game rather than a single-player snake, with the exact same three-mode start menu (Human vs Human, CPU vs Human, CPU vs CPU), green-on-black theme, WASD/Arrow-key dual controls, on-screen P1/P2 scores, and a food-seeking CPU AI (present in every file per grep of cpu/target/direction logic). No attempt diverges structurally or shows a broken/degraded implementation, so the run is stable in both approach and quality.

All six attempts converge on the same approach and comparable quality. All 6 attempts converge on the identical architecture: single self-contained HTML file, vanilla JS, localStorage key 'todos', a todos array + filter state, and render/save/load with data-filter buttons. Styling also varies cosmetically (no card in #1/#3, white card in #2/#4/#5/#6, green button + underlined-link filters in #5). All six attempts are clearly the same template: identical 8-vertex cube array, the same 6 quad faces split into two triangles via [0,1,2]/[0,2,3], hand-rolled vec3/dot/cross/normalize helpers, rotX/rotY built the same way, a 'z + distance' pseudo-perspective divide, a scanline Gouraud rasterizer that sorts the three vertices by y and lerps color per pixel, the same W/P keydown handler, and the same 1-second-window FPS counter with the exact same magic increments (angleX += 0.01, angleY += 0.013, lightAngle += 0.02) in every single file. Structure: attempt-06 abandons the scanline rasterizer for a barycentric per-pixel loop over getImageData/putImageData, and shades with a single flat face normal replicated to all three vertices (intensities = [lambert(faceNormal,L)] x3), so it isn't Gouraud at all - the requirement is silently dropped. Vertex normals differ elsewhere too: 01/02/05 average adjacent face normals, 04 approximates them as normalize(vertexPosition). Only 03 adds a painter's depth sort; the other five have no depth ordering, so faces overdraw arbitrarily. 02 uses a fixed 600x600 canvas with per-face base colors; the rest are fullscreen with one base color. 01/04 render on-screen key hints; 02/03/05/06 don't. Resulting quality is scattered across the screenshots: 01 has a projection scale bug (x * scale * aspect / z * cx) so the cube covers the whole viewport and per-pixel fillRect drops it to 1.3 FPS; 03 has the mirror-image bug - project() never multiplies by cx/cy - so the cube is a 2-pixel blue dot at 60 FPS; 04 shows two disconnected oversized quads at 4.7 FPS; 02 shows a single near-black sliver (inconsistent face winding plus normal[2]<0 culling) with FPS still reading 0; 05 renders a completely blank frame (culling against a camera at the origin while the cube is never translated away) at FPS 0; 06 shows flat, gradient-free oversized quads at 50 FPS. Not one of the six produces a recognizable shaded rotating cube, and each fails through a different bug in a different pipeline stage - projection scale, winding/culling, missing translation, shading model - so the approach is stable while the output is not.

All six attempts follow the same architecture: a single HTML file, 8 hard-coded cube vertices, per-axis rotateX/rotateY(/rotateZ) helpers applied vector-by-vector (none actually builds a 4x4 matrix), a divide-style perspective projection, quads split into two triangles, a Lambert term with an ambient offset, and a hand-written barycentric edge-function rasterizer that interpolates RGB per pixel; W/P key handlers and an FPS readout appear in every one. Only shot-01 shows anything on screen, and even there it is two detached grey quads rather than a cube (attempt-01 culls with dot(fn,[0,0,-1])>=0 against inconsistent face winding and has no depth resolution, so half the cube vanishes; it also strokes the wireframe with ctx.stroke() *before* ctx.putImageData, so the W toggle is invisible). shot-02, 04, 05 and 06 are entirely blank, again from distinct root causes: attempt-03 and attempt-05 mix units, using fov=400 with a cube of radius 1 (or 0.5) and no screen-space scale factor, so scale=400/(400+z)~0.99 projects the whole cube into a 1-2 pixel dot (visible as the single dark speck in the middle of shot-03); attempt-06 does angleX += 0.5*dt with dt = time*0.001 (absolute time, not a frame delta), so the angles accelerate quadratically and the cube strobes into garbage; attempt-02 and attempt-04 pass the *face* normal to all three vertices instead of averaged vertex normals, which is flat shading with a slight per-vertex light-direction variation rather than true Gouraud, and both invert the cull test relative to their winding. Secondary structural drift: attempt-02 rasterizes with one ctx.fillRect per pixel (thousands of draw calls/frame) while the others write into ImageData; attempt-05 does a getImageData/putImageData round-trip per triangle; attempts 05 and 06 add painter's-algorithm depth sorting that 01-04 omit; attempt-04 drops the ambient term entirely, so faces go fully black; base colors vary (grey, teal, orange, blue) and attempt-01/04 draw FPS on-canvas while 02/03 use a DOM overlay. Same recipe every time, wildly uneven execution of it - hence 0.5, not 1.

All six attempts converge on the same high-level architecture: a unit-cube vertex list, hand-written per-axis rotateX/Y/Z helpers, a divide-by-z perspective projection, dot-product backface culling, painter's-algorithm depth sort, quad-split-into-two-triangles, W/P key handlers and an FPS counter. Nothing here is structurally random. Crucially, the outcome is also uniform: not one of the six renders a visible cube (shots 01-06 are all empty canvases, at most showing the light-source dot and the HUD). Quality is therefore consistently zero in delivered output. What pushes this below 'stable' is that the core rasterizer and the failure mode vary substantially. Rasterization: 01, 03 and 06 write a genuine per-pixel barycentric loop; 02 writes a per-pixel scanline loop; 04 fakes it with a per-scanline ctx.createLinearGradient; 05 abandons rasterization and triangle-splitting entirely, drawing each quad as three vertices filled with one canvas gradient, which is not Gouraud at all. Lighting also diverges: only 04 averages adjacent face normals into true per-vertex normals, 02/03/05/06 reuse a single face normal for every vertex (flat shading in Gouraud clothing), and 01 abandons Lambert for an inverse-square distance falloff. The six break for six unrelated reasons, splitting into two visibly different behaviours. Three keep running at ~60 FPS while silently drawing nothing: 01 culls every face via 'if (faceVerts.some(v => v.z >= -fov)) continue' where z is in [-1.7,1.7] and fov is 400, so the test is always true; 02 never applies the intended x100 world scale, leaving a cube about 3 pixels wide; 03 has sign-flipped barycentric coordinates (u and v are both negated relative to the denominator), so the u<0 test rejects every interior pixel, and it also ships an abandoned barycentricInterpolation() that returns undefined with 'Wrong, fix below' left in the source. The other three hard-crash on frame one and report FPS 0: 04 assigns to a const in '[xLeft, xRight] = [xRight, xLeft]' (TypeError); 05 references an undefined lightIntensityZ3 typo; 06's sort comparator reads an undefined avgDepthB. In each of those three the exception escapes render() before requestAnimationFrame is rescheduled, so the loop dies permanently. Same blueprint and same uniformly broken result, but materially different rasterizer/lighting implementations and two distinct failure signatures across attempts.

All six attempts use the same intended Canvas 2D 3D-cube pipeline (rotations, projection, culling, moving light, Gouraud-style triangle rendering, W/P controls), but the implementations vary substantially and are unreliable. Visually, every screenshot lacks a rendered cube; attempts 01–03 show FPS around 60 with only a light dot, while 04–06 show FPS 0 or an otherwise blank canvas. The HTML implementations also differ greatly in size and rasterization/culling strategy, with clear defects such as attempt 05 referencing undefined lightIntensityZ3. This is a consistent overall approach with materially variable execution quality.

The six attempts share a genuinely uniform architecture — 8-vertex cube, quad face table split into two triangles, rotateX/rotateY (+Z in 01/06), perspective divide by (z+dist), backface cull, per-vertex Lambert with ambient ~0.10-0.15, painter's sort, manual rasterization into an ImageData buffer, W/P key toggles and a 1-second FPS counter — but the delivered results diverge from fully broken to good. attempt-03 renders NOTHING: shot-03 is a uniform dark field with not even its own green HUD text visible (it uses a per-triangle cross2D>0 cull with quad windings [0,3,2,1]/[4,5,6,7] and a directional-only light — everything is culled or the loop throws before `hud.textContent`), so it fails the task outright. attempt-01 is inverted: shot-01 shows the camera inside an enormous inside-out box filling the whole viewport, because its cull test `dot(faceNormal, viewDir) >= 0 -> skip` combined with its face windings keeps the far faces; it is the only attempt using a world-space normal/viewDir cull rather than a 2D screen-space cross product, and it is the one that gets it wrong. The four that work also differ substantially in framing and legibility: 01/02/03 size the canvas to window.innerWidth/Height, while 04 hardcodes 600x600, 05 720x540 and 06 800x600 — shot-04's cube is a ~100px speck and shot-05's is small and nearly black (only 2 faces above ambient), whereas shot-06 is a large, bright, cleanly shaded cube. Rasterizer choice is also split: barycentric edge functions (01, 05, 06) vs scanline edge-walking (02, 03, 04), and normals are split between smooth averaged vertex normals (01-05) and a single face normal reused per vertex (06, which weakens the Gouraud gradient to light-distance variation only). Two of six artifacts are non-functional and the working four range from a barely-visible speck to a polished render — that is random quality, not stable output.

The attempts vary wildly in visible outcome: attempt 03 is blank, attempt 01 renders an oversized clipped cube, attempts 04–05 render very small dim cubes, while attempts 02 and 06 show substantially larger cubes. Their implementations also differ materially (scanline vs. barycentric rasterizers, sizing/projection choices, and UI/status structures), so quality is not comparable across runs.

All six share a generic scaffold (8-vertex cube, quad faces split into triangles, painter's sort, HUD with FPS/W/P), but the substantive pipeline choices and the visual outcomes diverge sharply. Rasterizers differ in kind: attempts 01 and 06 fake Gouraud with a per-scanline ctx.createLinearGradient + fillRect; 02 does full-triangle barycentric interpolation over one getImageData/putImageData block; 03, 04, 05 build a per-scanline createImageData strip. Normals differ: 01, 02, 04, 05 accumulate/average face normals, while 03 and 06 shortcut to normalize(vertexPosition) (03 even keeps a computeFaceNormal helper it never uses, and 06 leaves a comment admitting the shortcut). Culling differs: fixed 3D viewDir [0,0,-1] (01), screen-space 2D cross product (02, 03, 04), per-face 3D view vector (05, 06 with the opposite sign). Lighting differs: 01 uses a directional light, the rest a point/orbiting light, with the light-marker projection hacked differently in each (03 computes `lightPos[2] - CAM_Z + CAM_Z`, 05 normalizes the light position then re-scales it by 3, 06 abandons projection entirely and draws the dot on a fixed 2D ellipse). The screenshots show the quality is effectively random rather than merely uneven: shot-02 is a correct, clearly Gouraud-gradient cube; shot-06 renders the cube inside-out (inverted cull sign — you see the interior walls, though colors interpolate); shot-05 is a solid cube but near-flat, over-saturated shading with almost no per-vertex gradient; shot-03 is a nearly black, barely-lit cube; shot-01 renders a single flat dark-green quad with no cube readable at all; shot-04 renders two disconnected slivers — the cube is destroyed. Two attempts are outright broken, one is inverted, one is too dark to read, one loses the Gouraud effect, and one is right. That is divergent, not variable-within-one-approach.

The attempts vary substantially in both rendering outcome and apparent pipeline correctness: 02 and 06 show coherent three-faced cubes, 01 renders only a single dark quadrilateral, 03 shows a small fragmented/partially visible cube, 04 has separated distorted polygons, and 05 has a severely skewed bright shape. The differing file sizes and hashes corroborate divergent implementations rather than stable repeated results.

The six attempts diverge wildly in both scope and correctness rather than varying in polish. Attempts 01, 02 and 05 (29.5k / 18.2k / 29.1k) are full spec-following builds: 8-item hour-by-hour timeline, 8 artist cards with an accessible modal (ESC + backdrop close), inline SVG map mock, the three specified tiers (Night/Curator/Patron, €29/€59/€129), 6+ FAQ items, newsletter, toasts, OG meta, and a client-side Blob .ics download. Attempts 04 (12.3k) and 06 (17.3k) are drastically reduced, partly re-invented pages: only 3 generic program cards with invented times (18:00–20:00 'Opening Night', 'Jazz & ambient'), 3 artists with no modal and no 'View details', no inline SVG map at all, and fabricated ticket tiers (04: 'Standard €30 / VIP €70' with an alert() instead of a checkout modal; 06: 'Standard $25 / VIP $50 / Collector $100'), 3 off-spec FAQ questions ('What is the dress code?'), no newsletter section, and no OG tags or data-URI SVG favicon. Attempt 04 also violates the headline special feature outright — no BEGIN:VCALENDAR anywhere; 'Save to Calendar' is a hardcoded external google.com/calendar/render link, not a generated .ics. Attempt 03 is functionally broken on load: the ticket modal is markup'd as `class="modal hidden"` but `.hidden` is never defined in its CSS (only attempt-01 defines `.modal.hidden{display:none}`), so a full-screen rgba(0,0,0,0.8) overlay plus an unstyled 'Confirm Ticket' form sits over the hero permanently — visible in shot-03, which shows the whole page dimmed and unusable. Attempt 06 also silently no-ops its scroll reveal (adds a `.visible` class with no matching rule). So across six runs the model produced three solid comparable builds, two heavily truncated off-spec rewrites, and one dead-on-arrival page — different approaches and wildly different quality.

The attempts vary substantially in completeness and polish: 01 and 05 are ~29 KB, include eight sections, nine images, and extensive modal code; 02–03 are smaller but broadly similar; 04 is only ~12 KB with five sections, four images, no modal implementation or Blob calendar download; 06 has six sections and four images. Screenshots also differ materially, including attempt 03 opening with a broken-looking/empty ticket modal and attempts 04/06 using simplified navigation and hero layouts. This is inconsistent quality rather than stable repeated execution.

The six attempts split into two incompatible families and vary wildly in spec fidelity and visual quality. Attempts 03-06 follow the brief closely: mandated ticket tiers Night/Curator/Patron at €29/€59/€129 (attempt-05:1132, attempt-04, attempt-06), the 8 named timeline items (Doors Open ... Closing Sound Session), a JS artists array of 8 objects with bio/role/session fields, a mobile nav toggle, and full SEO/OG/favicon meta. Attempts 01 and 02 ignore that content entirely: attempt-01:831-854 invents 'Standard Pass €45 / … €120 / Collector Pass €250', has zero occurrences of the required tier names or prices, none of the specified timeline entries, and swaps the mandated source.unsplash.com URLs for images.unsplash.com (10 uses); attempt-02 likewise invents tiers with per-card quantity steppers instead of the spec'd select-tier→modal flow, renders artists as a horizontal scroll-snap carousel with off-spec 300x300 'portrait,artist' images (attempt-02:1039-1041), and its <head> (lines 1-6) has no meta description, no Open Graph tags and no favicon at all — an entire required section missing that the other five all include. Rendering also diverges: hero is centered in 01/02/06 but left-aligned in 04/05; attempt-03's hero renders as a washed-out olive-brown box (shot-03) rather than velvet near-black, losing the cinematic direction; attempt-06's hero is flat pure black with no spotlight gradient and a small centered text block (shot-06), the weakest of the set; and attempts 05 and 06 both contain corrupted bytes where the en dash should be, rendering visibly as tofu — '19:00□02:00' (attempt-05:989) and worse '19:00□0:00' with the '2' lost (attempt-06:815). Scroll reveal is IntersectionObserver-based only in 01 and 02. So: different approaches, different content, missing requirement blocks in some attempts, and visible text-corruption defects in others — not comparable quality run to run.

All attempts use the same dark gold museum-night landing-page concept with the same core sections and calendar Blob download, but execution quality varies materially: attempt 01 has only 3 FAQ items and substitutes different ticket tiers; attempt 02 has only 5 artist cards and no detectable artist modal/ESC handling; attempts 03–06 more closely implement the requested 8-artist, 6-FAQ modal-driven structure. All six attempts converge on the same approach and land at comparable quality. Every attempt implements every required interaction — all 6 build the .ics with BEGIN:VCALENDAR + Blob download named artifact-museum-night.ics, all 6 have og:image + inline SVG data-URI favicon, all 6 use IntersectionObserver scroll reveal, ESC-closable modals, toast, FAQ accordion, inline SVG venue map, and all 6 render exactly 8 artist cards (01/05 via a JS data array, 02/03/04/06 as static markup — a minor implementation-style split, not a capability one). Even the deviations are shared rather than random: all 6 silently swap the prescribed source.unsplash.com URLs for hardcoded images.unsplash.com photo IDs, and 5 of 6 emit the identical DTSTART:20261018T170000Z UTC-shifted timestamp (02 templates the same value from a variable). Screenshots are visually interchangeable — same near-black/burgundy palette, same Georgia headline 'Museum Night, Reimagined' at the same scale, same left-text/right-image-card hero with date/time/place pills and Get Tickets + Save to Calendar CTAs; 05 and 06 differ only in wrapping the hero copy in a panel or swapping the floating caption for an info list. Nothing is broken in any attempt and none is a notable outlier in polish.

Five of six attempts (01, 03, 04, 05, 06) do converge: same single-file approach, same CSS-variable palette (#070506/#1a0710/#3a0f1d/#d6ad60), Georgia+Inter stacks, sticky nav with active state, IntersectionObserver scroll reveal, 8 artist cards + modal, inline SVG venue map, 3 ticket cards + checkout modal, FAQ accordion, newsletter, toast, and a Blob-based BEGIN:VCALENDAR .ics download; sizes cluster at 42–55KB. A 1-in-6 rate of shipping a truncated, JS-less, mostly non-functional page is wildly different quality, so this is divergent rather than merely variable.

All six attempts follow the same template and approach: identical section order and anchor ids (#program/#artists/#venue/#tickets/#faq, 6-7 <section> elements each), same sticky navbar + gold-on-near-black palette, same ICS-via-Blob implementation (BEGIN:VCALENDAR in all 6), and the same shared deviations from spec — every attempt swaps the required source.unsplash.com URLs for hand-picked images.unsplash.com photo IDs, every attempt prices tiers at €45/€85/€150 instead of €29/€59/€129, every attempt collapses the 8-item hour-by-hour timeline into ~3 blocks (19:00–20:30 / 21:00–23:30 / 23:30–02:00), none has the required 'View details' artist buttons, and 5 of 6 (02–06) use the exact same external url('https://grainy-gradients.vercel.app/noise.svg') instead of a CSS-only grain. That level of shared structure and shared error rules out divergence. Quality, however, varies clearly attempt to attempt, mostly via rendering/text defects: attempt-01's hero renders as flat black with no image and its subtitle is corrupted ('Museum Night, Reimag\t\t\t...imaged', with a matching tab-run corrupting one image URL at line 553); attempt-06 shows a garbled date, '18 October 202 nghiệm 26' (line 452); attempt-03 renders the ARTIFACT logo as default unstyled link blue and misspells the headline 'Reimaged'; attempt-04 leaves all five nav links unstyled blue-underlined and ships only 2 remote images total vs 4-6 in the others; attempt-05 scrambles the tier price order (€45 / €120 / €75). Attempt-02 is the only visually clean one. Feature coverage also drifts: only attempt-01 includes an inline SVG favicon, and no attempt includes the required inline SVG venue map. Same recipe every time, meaningfully different execution quality.

All attempts use the same dark burgundy/black-and-gold museum-event landing-page pattern with a sticky nav, oversized serif hero, program, artists, tickets, FAQ, modals, and calendar download. All six attempts take the same approach and are near-identical structurally: one self-contained HTML file, same section order (sticky nav → hero → concept → timeline → artists → venue → tickets → FAQ → newsletter → footer), the same prescribed palette/serif+sans stacks, 8 artist cards (attempt-03 generates them from a JS array, the rest hardcode 'View details' 8×), a BEGIN:VCALENDAR Blob download in all 6, IntersectionObserver for active-nav + scroll reveal in all 6, an inline SVG map mock plus SVG data-URI favicon, og:image meta in all 6, and 3 ticket tiers with a validating checkout modal and toasts. File sizes cluster tightly (22–33 KB). The divergence is in rendered quality, not architecture: attempt-02 renders a completely blank hero — it puts the `reveal` class (opacity:0/translateY) on the hero <section> itself, so the headline, event name, date line and both CTAs are invisible on load, failing the 'hero looks cinematic' criterion outright. Among the working ones, hero polish still varies noticeably: 04, 05 and 06 have well-spaced gold/ivory hierarchy with distinct button styling, 03 renders a flatter navy hero with a plain white headline and a visible hard-edged diagonal artifact, and 01 pushes the hero content low with a large empty top band and low-contrast secondary CTA. All rely on gradient fallbacks since the source.unsplash URLs no longer resolve, which is uniform across attempts. Consistent approach, variable quality — one attempt visually broken.

All six attempts use the same dark-and-gold ARTIFACT single-page layout, matching hero copy, navbar, sections, ticket/calendar interactions, and broadly comparable visual treatment. Quality is nevertheless variable: attempt 02 renders an almost entirely blank hero beneath the navbar, while the other five render the headline and CTAs; implementation sizes also vary materially (about 22 KB to 33 KB), and attempt 05 contains duplicated modal/total functions. This is a consistent overall approach with notable execution instability, not fully stable.

All six attempts converge on the same approach and skeleton: single self-contained HTML, identical section order (nav → hero → [concept] → program → artists → venue → tickets → faq → newsletter → footer), the same near-black/burgundy + gold serif-headline aesthetic, the same hero copy ('Museum Night, Reimagined' / 'ARTIFACT: Museum Night' / 18 October 2026, 19:00–02:00, The Old Gallery Warsaw), the same sticky navbar with the five required links, and the same client-side .ics-via-Blob implementation (BEGIN:VCALENDAR present in all 6). All six also make the same deviation from the brief in the same direction: none uses the mandated source.unsplash.com URLs — every attempt swaps in images.unsplash.com photo IDs — and none uses the specified tier names or prices. So the *method* is stable. Completeness and polish, however, swing a lot between runs. Artist cards (acceptance criterion says 8): attempt-01 = 8, 02 = 8, 04 = 8, but 03 = 4, 06 = 4, 05 = 3. Program timeline (spec: 8 hour-by-hour entries with location tags): 01 = 6, 04 = 6, 02 = 5, 03 = 4, 06 = 4, 05 = 5 — and 05 renders it as a card grid, not a vertical timeline, with no location tags anywhere. SEO/meta is wildly inconsistent: attempt-01 alone has the full set (description + og:title/og:description/og:image + inline SVG data-URI favicon), 04 has partial OG tags, and 02/03/05/06 have neither OG tags nor a favicon. Ticket tiers are re-invented each run: 01 = Standard/Premium/VIP Platinum €89/189/399, 02 = Standard/Premium/VIP €45/75/150, 03 = Standard/Premium/Collector €45/75/150, 04 = Standard/Premium/Exclusive €45/75/150, 05 = €45/85/150, 06 = Gallery Access/Premium Experience/Platinum Patron 49/99/199. Attempt-05 is a clear outlier on top of that: 47KB vs 64–77KB for the rest, no inline SVG venue map at all (the other five all ship a <svg viewBox='0 0 400 400'> map mock), no artist modal (openArtistModal exists in 01/02/03/04/06 only), no newsletter section, and its hero is the only split left/right layout — with a fabricated Unsplash photo ID that 404s, so shot-05 shows a visibly broken image placeholder where every other screenshot shows a clean cinematic hero. Attempt-04 also drifts stylistically, using emoji (📅🕐📍) for hero metadata badges where the others use typographic DATE/TIME/LOCATION labels, and has a duplicate id attribute (id="tickets" id="ticketsSection"). Screenshots 01–04 and 06 are visually near-interchangeable; 05 is plainly a lesser artifact. Consistent approach, materially variable quality and feature coverage — 0.5, not 1 (05's three missing required features and broken image, plus the 8-vs-3 artist-card spread, are too large) and not 0 (structure, styling, and technique are otherwise the same every run).

The six attempts share only a rough skeleton (two snakes, three modes, greedy Manhattan-distance CPU) and diverge substantially in both structure and working state. Rendering differs: attempts 01-04 and 06 draw on a 600x600 <canvas>, while attempt-05 abandons canvas entirely for a CSS-grid of 900 <div> cells. The menu mechanism differs: attempt-01 draws its menu inside the canvas and starts with keys 1/2/3, attempts 02/03/04/06 use HTML button overlays, attempt-05 has buttons that are never wired to any listener (only keys 1/2/3 work). Restart differs too: 'any key' (01, 03), 'R' (02, 05, 06), a button (04). Quality is not comparable across runs. Attempt-01 and attempt-03 are broadly playable. Attempt-02 is dead on arrival: `#menu{display:none}` in CSS and nothing ever unhides it, so the game can never be started (screenshot shows only an empty black canvas); it also spawns both snakes on the identical center cell. Attempt-04 also spawns both snakes at the same center cell with dir {0,0}, so head1===head2 on tick one and human-vs-human ends instantly. Attempt-05 leaves the dark #overlay visible after startGame (it only hides #menu/#gameOver), and calls `new Snake(mode===2||mode===1,false,'snake2')` with a shifted argument, so the color class is wrong; its screenshot shows menu and Game Over text stacked on top of each other simultaneously. Attempt-06 is not even a clean artifact: ~35 lines of raw chain-of-thought planning prose are emitted before the doctype and render as visible text above the game (clearly seen in shot-06). That spread — two mostly-working files, two with instant-death or unreachable-start bugs, one with a different rendering technology and dead buttons, one with leaked reasoning text — is divergent rather than merely variable in polish.

All six attempts follow the same recipe: a single self-contained HTML file, CSS custom properties using the exact specified palette (#070506 / #3a0f1d / #d6ad60 …), Georgia serif headlines with the identical 'Museum Night, / Reimagined' two-line lockup, sticky nav with the same section set, IntersectionObserver scroll reveals, a data-driven artist array + modal, FAQ accordion, ticket-tier cards with a checkout modal, and an ICS Blob download (all 6 contain BEGIN:VCALENDAR and a temporary-link download). None used the specified source.unsplash URLs — every attempt substituted images.unsplash photo IDs, a consistent deviation. Quality, however, varies substantially. Attempt 02 (44 KB, half the size of the median) is the clear outlier: only 4 artist cards instead of the required 8, no toast system at all — it uses browser alert() for ticket confirmation and newsletter signup (lines 1164, 1238) — no Escape-key close, no aria-modal on its dialogs, no image in the artist modal, and its hero photo is a bright multicolour painting that reads nothing like 'velvet darkness'. Attempt 03 (51 KB) drops the required hero image entirely, rendering a pure CSS gradient + blurred spotlight blobs instead. At the other end, 01 (112 KB), 05 (117 KB) and 04 (90 KB) are polished, near-identical split-layout heroes with a dark gallery photo, 8 artists, full toast/ESC/aria-modal handling and 17–25 remote images; 06 (63 KB) sits in between with a full-bleed hero. Layout also splits into two families — asymmetric image-right (01, 04, 05) vs centred text (02, 03, 06) — and several screenshots (02, 04, 06) show the nav 'GET TICKETS' label rendering gold-on-gold and effectively unreadable. Same architecture and design language every time, but the feature completeness and visual execution range from premium to visibly deficient.
